Why Texas

No state on earth is built for solar like Texas.

With more than 300 sunny days a year, a deregulated energy market, and some of the most favorable commercial tax incentives in the country, going solar in Texas isn't just smart — it's the natural next move for any business serious about its long-term costs.

Longhorn Solar brings commercial and industrial solar expertise to Texas operations of every size — from single-facility rooftop deployments to multi-site campus ground-mount configurations. We design, deploy, and monitor everything so you can focus on running your operation.

And because Longhorn Solar is a Seebury company, your system can be integrated into a broader DESAEAT multiservice energy strategy — pairing solar with gas backup, Tesla Megapack storage, or waste-to-energy depending on what your environment actually demands.

Texas's vast open landscape, intense sun, and wind resources make it the nation's premier commercial solar environment.

Our Technology

Solar Sentinel

Always Watching. Always Optimizing.

Solar Sentinel is Longhorn Solar's proprietary monitoring and optimization platform — giving you real-time visibility into your system's performance from any device, at any time.

Most solar companies install and walk away. We stay. Solar Sentinel means a Longhorn Solar engineer is watching your system around the clock, catching issues before they become outages and continuously tuning for maximum output.

  • Predictive maintenance alerts before failures occur

Reference Projects

At Scale. In the Ground.

Longhorn Solar designs for Texas realities — from rooftop commercial to utility-scale floating solar on reservoir and water body assets.

Floating Solar 248 MWp Ciel & Terre Platform

Hidalgo County Reservoir

South Texas · Floating PV · Ciel & Terre aiR 1280

One of the largest floating solar installations in the United States — a 248.38 MWp floating photovoltaic plant deployed across the Hidalgo County Reservoir using 451,602 PV modules on the Ciel & Terre aiR 1280 platform at a 5° reversed duo pitch configuration.

The project comprises 34 individual floating solar arrays ranging from 1.5 to 19 acres each, spanning array capacities from ~1.0 MW to 11.7 MW. The floating platform reduces water evaporation, improves panel efficiency through surface cooling, and adds dual-use value to existing water infrastructure — no farmland consumed, no ground disturbance.

Seebury and Longhorn Solar deploy floating solar on reservoirs, retention ponds, irrigation lakes, and industrial water bodies across Texas — paired with grid interconnect, battery storage, or DESAEAT multiservice energy configurations as required.

The Problem Nobody Is Talking About

2.2 Million Tons
of Wind Blades
in U.S. Landfills by 2050.

This photograph was taken at the Casper Regional Landfill in Wyoming. Wind turbine blades — built to last 20–25 years — are being buried whole. Hundreds of them. Every year. The wind industry created the problem. Seebury helped find the solution.

Carbon Rivers · Knoxville, Tennessee
Seebury Wind Services

Wind Turbine Blade Recycling — The Solution Is Here.

Wind turbine blades have historically been constructed from composite materials — polymers reinforced with glass or carbon fibers — engineered for strength, not recyclability. As the first generation of U.S. wind farms reaches end of life, decommissioned blades are being landfilled at scale.

Seebury has partnered with Carbon Rivers of Knoxville, Tennessee — the company that cracked the composites recycling problem. Their process recovers high-value fiber from turbine blades and repurposes it as industrial feedstock, keeping the material out of landfills permanently.

This is not a future technology. It is operational now — and Longhorn Solar brings it to Texas wind operators who need a decommissioning path that doesn't end at a landfill gate.

Carbon Rivers — The Circular Economy for Composites
Knoxville, Tennessee · Partner Technology

Composites — the marriage of performance fibers with polymer matrices — are engineering marvels with one serious flaw: they resist conventional recycling. Carbon Rivers' breakthrough process recovers the fiber content from decommissioned blades at commercial scale, converting a waste stream into a premium industrial material.

2.2M
Tons to U.S. landfills by 2050
20–25
Year blade lifespan — decommissioning now
Recycling Partner: Carbon Rivers — Knoxville, Tennessee
Certified Small Business · DOE-Funded · University of Tennessee & Oak Ridge National Laboratory

Carbon Rivers has commercialized the only currently available technology that can recycle fiberglass from decommissioned wind turbine blades — recovering clean, mechanically intact glass fiber at 99.9% purity. Their Glass to Glass Reclamation process converts end-of-life blades into high-quality glass fiber that can be reincorporated into the next generation of turbine blades, automotive panels, marine vessels, and construction materials — creating a truly circular economy for composites.

The Seebury 6D Development Process is the answer — a disciplined six-stage methodology that takes every project from initial site discovery through long-term facility defense and continuous improvement.

Strategic Partnering

Alliances Built to Last.

Strategic partnering is something everyone talks about — rarely are these relationships developed in a successful manner. At Seebury we seek to develop successful joint ventures and project consortia that deliver value to all participants. No organization can do everything.

The Seebury Partnership Equation
(SR)3 + (SV)2 = High Effectiveness

Effective partnerships are a precise combination of Shared Risk, Shared Resources, Shared Rewards, Shared Vision, and Shared Values. Without each element, the alliance is unbalanced — and an unbalanced partnership sows the seeds of distrust.

(SR)³ — The Three Shared Rs
Shared Risk — Each partner bears a fair and appropriate share of risk. No partner carries a disproportionate burden.
Shared Resources — Each commits an appropriate proportion — capital, people, knowledge, or technology.
Shared Rewards — Partners work together to create mutual wins. No partner takes all the upside.
(SV)² — The Two Shared Vs
Shared Vision — Partners hold a common view of objectives, results, and outcomes. They share an understanding of what the alliance is for.
Shared Values — Common value systems and complementary cultures. This is the bedrock — providing the means, motivation, and commitment to resolve problems and grow the relationship.
